title: A split invoice gives the Labor rep a Labor row and the Parts rep a Parts row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 0%, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour (Tech Time 2.00) and one part sold at $50.00; "Sales Representative - Labor" reads {Sales-rep-A} and "Sales Representative - Parts" reads {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice {Work-order-1}.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative, set the date range to today, turn Show Unassigned on and turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  3. Read {Sales-rep-A}'s invoice row for {Work-order-1}.
  4. Read {Sales-rep-B}'s invoice row for {Work-order-1}.
  5. Read each representative's summary row and invoice count.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice is created.
  • Step 2: the report shows two rows for {Work-order-1}'s invoice, one under {Sales-rep-A} and one under {Sales-rep-B}; the Sales Type column shows after Status.
  • Step 3: Sales Type "Labor"; Labor Invoiced $200.00, Hrs Invoiced 2.00, labor columns filled; Parts Invoiced and Parts Margin show a dash, not $0.00.
  • Step 4: Sales Type "Parts"; Parts Invoiced $50.00; Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta and Shop Supplies show a dash.
  • Step 5: each summary row shows real sums (no dashes): {Sales-rep-A} $200.00 of labor, {Sales-rep-B} $50.00 of parts; each counts the invoice once.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10890; story SV-11266 (Story 2, Give a work order a separate Labor and Parts representative); story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative); PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 8 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R1, S5-R3, S5-R4, S5-R5, S5-R11, S5-R13, S5-R15, S5-R16, S5-R19, S2-R13, read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. The build is not yet available to check this case against.

The Sales By Representative spec, version 28 (12 Oct 2026, S9-N1), shows Labor Delta as 0.0 on a Parts row, and it also places Location right after Status (S18-R13). PRD version 8 (14 Oct 2026) is later and says a dash; this case follows the PRD, which we take as prevailing. Both points are on the product owner's question list.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R1: “When a work order is invoiced, the parts representative and the labor representative in effect are both captured on the invoice, by name.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”
  • S5-R4: “A Labor row is credited with Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, labor-line fees and discounts, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta and all of the invoice's Shop Supplies, including an amount typed by hand.”
  • S5-R5: “A Parts row is credited with Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin and part-line fees and discounts.”
  • S5-R11: “Two different people on one work order are always two rows.”
  • S5-R13: “A representative counts an invoice once, even when they have two rows for it. When two people split an invoice, each counts it once, so the representatives' invoice counts can add up to more than the shop's.”
  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero.”
  • S5-R16: “A representative's summary row always shows real sums, never dashes.”
  • S5-R19: “An invoice row carries a "Sales Type" column, after Status, reading "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" or "Labor, Parts".”
  • S2-R13: “"Sales Representative - Labor" is credited with the labor side of the invoice and "Sales Representative - Parts" with the parts side (Story 5).”
